notes: The whole 98-page final PDF, read end to end: the introduction, purpose and methodology, the three-part historic context (first-wave immigration 1910-1940, the war and its aftermath 1941-1964, second-wave immigration 1965-present), the sections on urban renewal, social support organisations, educational facilities, businesses, the Yerba Buena redevelopment, the Filipino-associated street renamings, Victoria Manalo Draves Park, arts and cultural celebrations, the report's own table of Filipino social heritage resources, the references, the oral history summaries in Appendix A, and the reprinted 2011 Western SoMa Citizens Planning Task Force document in Appendix B with its own three appendices. Two seams carry nearly everything: the report's resources table on pp. 38-39, which gives a name, an address, an assessor's block and lot and a date of origin for each; and the narrative, which reads city directories year by year and so puts a named organisation or business at a numbered address on a dated line over and over.

coverage.remaining: None. The report and both its appendices are read in full.
coverage.note: 120 numbered-address mentions across 98 pages, on 115 distinct addresses, plus 33 more recorded from the whole of Appendix B's Appendix 3 survey table, which is now read in full. Appendix A, the oral history summaries, was read in full and yielded nothing: it records where people lived, worked and went to school, which the privacy limits bar, and the buildings it names are named in the report body too. One narrative address was dropped for the same reason — a 1930 census entry giving a named individual's family home. Appendix B is a different document reprinted whole: the Western SoMa Citizens Planning Task Force's 2011 draft. Its own Appendix 3 is a survey table with an assessor's block and lot on most rows; every row carrying a street number is now a finding, and the parcel cross-check came back 40 exact, 13 re-lotted since and 0 on another block. What the table cannot support is a dated event: its YEAR BUILT column reproduces the assessor's build year on the rows dated before about 1960 — it matches the 2025 roll on twelve of the fifteen rows where the roll carries one — while the asset beside it is the use standing in 2011, so the two are not one fact. Five entries published from it in PR #199 were withdrawn for exactly that, and the pre-1960 rows are declined as a class. Eleven rows of the table carry no street number at all — the five 1980 street renamings, two murals, a community garden on Lapu Lapu Street and four street festivals — and are not findings.
